steps: The front desk types up notes and prints the e-mails.
The warden checks them against the calendar.
The warden writes the bookings in.
The front desk replies to each group.
The treasurer raises an invoice from each confirmed booking in the calendar.
problems: Twice last term the Garden Room was given to two groups at once.
Notes left at the front desk wait a week before anyone types them.
The treasurer invoices from the calendar, so a wrong booking becomes a wrong invoice.
cites: [A:A01 "twice last term the Garden Room was given to two groups at once"]

confidence.high: The row quotes the request line that decided it, and the calendar entry it clashes with when there is one.
confidence.medium: A reputable secondary source; not expected here.
confidence.low: Inferred or one weak source, such as a note that gives a day but no date; such a row is refused and raised as a question.

conflicts: The higher rank wins within its own area.
A conflict the ranks do not settle is reported with both citations, never decided silently.

output.description: One row per request, with a decision: propose, clash or refuse. A request with no room or no time is refused as incomplete; a request for more people than the room holds is refused with the room's limit.

risk.notes: A wrong booking can be cancelled, but a group that turns up to a double-booked room has lost its evening. Outside groups are affected; the treasurer may also raise a wrong invoice from a wrong booking, which then has to be cancelled by hand. Nothing reaches the calendar before the warden approves. A request over a room's limit that slipped through would breach the fire certificate, which is why such requests are refused outright rather than proposed with a warning.
cites: [A:A01 "Partly reversible"]
[A:A02 "Around fifty outside groups a year, plus the treasurer, who invoices from the calendar."]
